content.thinking:
I'm planning the overall design: a koala sized around 0.65 meters sitting, clinging to a vertical eucalyptus branch mounted on a base stand, with limbs positioned naturally around the trunk.

I'm working through the exact geometry so the koala appears to be hugging the trunk realistically, placing the body, head, and reaching arms so they wrap around the trunk's surface without clipping through it, while making sure the base touches the ground.

I'm now laying out the skeleton structure: hips rooted near the ground, a spine chain running up through the torso, and a neck chain connecting to the head, each defined by explicit points so the limbs can grip the trunk naturally.

I'll place the jaw joint under the head using absolute coordinates to avoid orientation confusion, defining head as a sphere and jaw as a small box beneath the snout. For the body, I'll sweep a mesh along the spine chain's path with varying radii to form the torso shape.

For the radius profile I'll use a pear-shaped function with values like [0.15, 0.165, 0.14] to give the koala body its taper. I'm painting fur gray with dithering, using a cell-shading approach based on surface normals so front-facing chest areas appear creamy white, and adding a texel-based pixel style at 0.025 resolution for the fur texture.

I'm deciding on a chunky voxel-style construction: using boxes for the head instead of spheres to keep the pixel-art look, with a box geometry roughly 0.22x0.19x0.2 for the head shape, and planning stepped outline extrusions for round fluffy ears with a smaller pale inner-ear patch.

Now I'm positioning the nose: a big black oval box protruding from the front of the snout, placed where the head box's front face sits, making it prominent like a koala's nose.

For the eyes, I'm using small black boxes with a pixel-art glint texture to add a tiny white highlight, keeping the grid simple with a few pixels of contrast.

Then I'm setting up the jaw as a separate bone box positioned lower on the face for the mouth.

For the muzzle, I'm adding a cream-colored box that overlaps the head to form the upper lip area, plus a thin dark line for the mouth seam. For fur, I'm planning to scatter tufted texture cards across the head and body using the surface sweep, with randomized placement, size, and lean angle to give a fluffy, pixelated look.

Now I'm working out the arm chains, placing shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints so the hands wrap naturally around the trunk, adjusting x-coordinates so the wrist sits just outside the trunk radius. Each arm is a three-point chain with tapering sweep radii and fur-colored skin, and I'm starting to think through how the koala's hand fingers should be structured as a smaller sub-chain.

Still writing finger wrapping geometry...

I'm adding spiked claws at the fingertips using the tangent direction, plus a dark gray fur sphere at the wrist for the hand base. Then I'm working out the leg joint positions from hip to knee to ankle to foot, positioning the foot center relative to the trunk's x-range.

For the feet, I'll reuse the wrapping function to create four front toes and one rear big toe around the ankle area, and I'm checking that the body and trunk surfaces leave a reasonable gap so nothing overlaps.

Adjusting positions so the koala appears hugging the trunk: I'm moving the trunk closer and shrinking the chest/spine so the chest front stays clear of the trunk surface, then repositioning the arms and head accordingly so everything stacks without intersecting.

Shifting trunk depth further forward, adjusting arm and leg joint positions to reach the new surface, and now sketching a wooden plinth base for the trunk stand.

Working out the trunk stand base and curved trunk shape, with a slight lean using catmull points and tapered radius, plus a bark texture using cell-paint streaks for vertical grain detail.

I need a proper joint hierarchy: a root "base" joint, with hips as the spine's parent joint. Then I'm adding side branches off the trunk at different heights with eucalyptus leaf cards—long oval pixel-art textures in green shades, arranged along each branch sweep using frame collection along the bone.

Placing leaf cards at multiple angles around each branch point...

Still placing branch coordinates...

Now I'm setting up the stand base with a wood plank texture, then moving to the fur shading—using a dithered ramp from dark to light gray with noise-based variation, plus adjustments for the belly/chest area to look lighter.

Writing fur paint logic...

Working out the inner ear positioning nested inside the outer ear shape, then placing ears on the head sides near the top. Now I'm adding cheek tufts as pale white boxes on the sides of the head for coloring detail.

Positioning the small eye boxes on the head front face with a slight protrusion, deciding to skip brow details since texture handles eye sparkle. Koalas have no tail, so I'm just adding a small rump bump and dark cream claws, then setting up the hip and leg bone chains parented correctly to the spine.

Still writing the spine chain and joint hierarchy...

Computing finger wrap positions...

Working out toe and foot placement, adding dark pad spheres at the ankles, and adjusting leg heights to suggest a climbing pose with offset feet. Now I'm tallying up the full joint hierarchy needed for the skeleton, including spine, limbs, and finger chains.

Trimming the finger/toe chains down to two joints each to keep the total joint count comfortably under budget, and setting up the chain-building logic to pass ordered point lists through a Catmull-Rom spline for smooth limb curves. I'm also checking the facial geometry, making sure the nose box sits forward of the snout surface without poking through the trunk.

Now I'm placing the snout as a cream box on the head bone, adding a jaw part with its own joint positioned to aim toward the mouth opening, and a thin dark strip to suggest the mouth line between upper and lower jaw.

Setting up the neck and head joint chain parented from the spine, then I'm thinking through the body sweep -- using a pear-shaped radius profile that's wider at the hips and narrower toward the chest, following the spine chain with rounded caps.

Designing fur tuft texture...

Still writing leaf pixel art...

For the base I'm adding wood-textured planks, scattered leaf litter, and small brown gum nuts on branches. I'm also adding dark bark knot nubs onto the trunk using small boxes placed along the trunk's sweep curve.

I'm setting up bone attachments for the trunk stand and branches so the cards and leaf frames inherit the correct weights, then double-checking the sweep point types and color parameter formats (string vs Paint) before writing the fur paint function.

The fur function uses layered noise plus directional lighting based on surface normal to brighten the chest/front and darken the back, with occasional random dark flecks for texture variation, and I'm tuning the ramp to include a near-white highlight near the top. I'm applying lighter chest values for limbs and a slightly stronger one for the head before moving on to the cell paint sizing.

Now I'm figuring out the texel density needed for a roughly 1.2 m² painted surface to keep detail crisp without being wasteful, settling on about 1.3mm texels with a coarser 20mm cell grid, and using a 0.02 texel size for box geometry. For bark, I'm blending stretched noise fields to create vertical striping plus a secondary noise pass to carve out pale peeling patches, picking colors off a bark ramp and using THREE.Vector3 for the stretched coordinates. Now I'm starting a pixel texture function for wood that lays out plank rows.

Writing plank pixel logic... I'm deciding to instantiate all the procedural generators (noise, rng, etc.) inside the build() function rather than at module scope, since that's where everything should live according to the generation pattern. I'm also working out the tiling math for the base box against its 32x16 texture, then adjusting the vertical layout so the base, trunk, and feet all sit cleanly above the floor without clipping, and finalizing export metadata like name, description, style, and commit hash alongside the default build export.

Now I'm setting up the imports needed for the koala build file -- pulling in the builder, frame helper, rng, path and paint utilities, sweep types, and pixel kit functions like tileBox and pixelArt -- then starting the build function itself by creating the builder instance, seeding the rng, defining a texel constant, and beginning to lay out the joint hierarchy starting with the base and hips.

Now I'm sketching out fur card textures using pixelArt patterns with tinted palette colors, then scattering these as surface cards across the body with randomized placement and size constraints, before moving into a helper function for wrapping digit/limb segments with configurable radius and color.

Writing wrap helper function...

Refining the color parameter type to accept Paint objects, using the same approach for leg toes as limbs.

Now building the arm chains for each side with shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints positioned using catmull-rom curves...

Adding sweep radii, hand sphere geometry, and finger/thumb wrap bones...

Now I'm setting up the leg chain with hip, knee, and ankle joints, parenting them under the hips with proper roles and contact points.

Defining the branch sweep function...

I'm checking whether casting the frame type for the flow callback is safe, and considering just using a fixed outward-and-upward direction vector for the branch tip instead of relying on the cast.

Simplifying by dropping the SweepPoint import and typing frames array via the sweep's own return type instead. Now I'm sketching out gumnut placement using sphere geometry attached to bones via frames, and starting to define the branch coordinate lists.

I'm checking branch B3's path against the koala's head and hands -- its forward trajectory toward +z would collide with where the hands wrap around the trunk, so I need to redirect that branch away from the front.

Placing branch four low on the right side, then defining the trunk's overall sweep path with its tapering radius up to the head area, and adding a top leaf cluster with cards angled around the trunk's upper section at a 40-degree lean.

Now I'm scattering leaf litter around the base, placing random-facing frames near ground level and attaching leaf cards to them with randomized flow directions for a natural scattered look.

Writing wood texture code...

Skipping extra chunky back boxes, and adding cheek fluff with a light cream fur ramp near the head bone. I'm also noting type imports for the Paint type and making sure the sweep radius parameter accepts a number array for the wrap geometry.

Checking that the chain's contact option is valid, then adding a small spike for a claw using the base/tip/length/radius signature before writing it out.
